query_trail: Zenodo API public query: ("actuator saturation" OR "windup") AND resource_type.type:dataset; first page (size 25) returned the two-tank record. Inspected version and concept metadata, associated Scientific Data article, archived README and CHANGELOG, fixed acquisition scripts, and both original ZIP bundles.

Wider queries: "anti-windup"; ("clipped" OR "saturation") AND ("motor controller" OR "servomotor"). The Segway-like anti-windup paper 10.1016/j.automatica.2024.111830 Figure 2/section 6.3 reports blue physical traces and orange simulation on a separate scale. Its command is a voltage reference implemented using PWM; no separately downloadable numerical run was identified here. The adaptive BIC paper 10.1109/LCSYS.2023.3282378 tests the controller using simulations. Neither source supplies the pump recordings.
coverage: 25 physical, scalar feedback-controlled pump/upper-tank experiments with a lower reservoir. 30,600 samples per trial, 765,000 total (nominally 1 Hz). Version 2 is a corrected representation of the same acquisitions. Each of 25 v2 members matched a single v1 member by a hash of the binary64 values of level, logged command, setpoint, error, Kp, a1, a2, b1; complete member SHA-256 for both versions are separately recorded. Four wholly empty trailing v1 rows were excluded. Each file is one run. Keep fixed v2 valve-opening labels and names; see CHANGELOG for the high-outflow relabeling.
acquisition: The MATLAB program reads the level, updates error and RLS coefficients, computes incremental self-tuning PID, clips each request to [0,100] percent, sends a separately rounded 8-bit serial command, and logs the clipped percentage. The first two rows use a distinct fallback controller. Pre-limit control is reconstructed, not recorded separately. The released Arduino firmware is a reconstruction: physical PWM timing, pin assignments, terminal voltage, speed and pump current are not verified by the logs.
formulas: For k≥3 in one-based indexing and nominal T=1 s, use u(k-1) from the logged clipped command. Unguarded request = u(k−1) + Kp*Δe + Ki*e(k) + Kd*Δ²e. Independently use original RLS coefficients with Q=1−exp(−1/3): u(k−1) + Q/b1 * [−(a1+2*a2)*Δe + (1+a1+a2)*e(k) + a2*Δ²e]. Both use the same measured errors and prior command; they are two numerical routes through the same controller equations. The gain route uses the corrected Ki/Kd, and v1 had accidentally interchanged Ti/Td during logging. Original DAQ command did not use v1’s mistaken *logged* gain values.
thresholds: An upper or lower clipped event is called when both reconstructions exceed the same bound by >0.01 percentage points and the separately logged post-limiter command equals that bound exactly. This 0.01 is an analysis tolerance for rounded inputs. Also report independently the maximum post-clip mismatch per file, the remaining endpoint rows, and simultaneous Sensor_Dropout flags. Extreme pre-limit values are algebraic requests under the supplied coefficients, not physical pump capabilities.
results: Of 764,950 adaptive rows, 1,144 met the lower criterion and 200,314 the upper. A further 26 logged 100% rows did not clear the dual 0.01 threshold. No dual-threshold exceedance occurred with an output off the expected rail. Re-clipping coefficient-replayed requests agrees within 0.000092 percentage points on every adaptive row. Re-clipping the corrected-gain replay gives 7 errors >0.01 (maximum 0.051781). 13,607 upper-bound and 446 lower-bound rows coincide with the authors’ zero-level-after-fill flag. These flags describe sensor dropouts, not causal attribution for the limit events. Across the full 765,000 recorded commands, host DAQ_Write rounding would assign unsigned byte 255 to 200,904 rows, including 564 below 100 percent. It would assign byte 0 to 1,153 rows, including 9 above 0 percent. These bytes are reconstructed from published percentages, not a separate capture or terminal voltage measurement.
time: Time_s is a regular sample index supplied in v2. Wall-clock timestamps have limited resolution including duplicate minute-stamped values in baseline runs. Analyses use record order, keep flagged dropouts because the physical controller consumed them, and do not interpret repeated clock labels as duplicate samples.
reproduction: Python 3 + numpy + pandas: download Dataset.zip and Dataset_v2.zip from releases, then python derive_two_tank.py Dataset.zip Dataset_v2.zip OUT. Output contains per-file independent summaries only.
